__comment: The shared Scrap Network workstation shape: a bench top on four short legs.
One model, three blocks. The Scrap Crafting Table, the Sorting Tarp and the Teardown Workbench
are the blocks a player lines up into a cluster, and two of them used to be plain cubes while
the third was a table - so a row of them read as three unrelated objects rather than one
workstation. Children override only the four texture slots.
THE TOP SPANS THE FULL 16 AND THAT IS THE POINT. It was 1..15, which left a pixel of daylight
on each side and a two-pixel gap between neighbours, so adjacent stations never visually
touched and the cluster did not read as one surface. Legs stay inset; only the worktop is flush.
Any block using this needs noOcclusion() - it is not a full cube, and without it the game still
culls the neighbouring block's face and you see straight through the ground.
The Java collision shape lives in WorkstationTable.SHAPE and must match these boxes.

elements.__comment: worktop - full width so a row of stations forms one continuous surface
